questions.title: Which structure does the stria medullaris thalami connect the septal area to?
questions.question: The stria medullaris thalami is a white-matter bundle that connects the septal area to which structure?

explanations.A: Correct. The stria medullaris thalami runs along the dorsomedial margin of the thalamus and carries fibres from the septal area (and other limbic forebrain structures) to the habenular nucleus. This makes it one of the principal inputs of the habenulo-limbic system. From the habenular nucleus, the habenulointerpeduncular tract continues on to link the limbic forebrain with brainstem monoaminergic centres.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The septal area connects to the mammillary bodies chiefly via the fornix, not the stria medullaris thalami, which specifically targets the habenular nucleus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. It is the stria terminalis, a separate tract, that connects the amygdala to the hypothalamus — not the stria medullaris thalami, which links the septal area to the habenular nucleus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The stria medullaris thalami's target is the habenular nucleus, not the hypothalamus directly.

questions.learning_objective: State that the stria medullaris thalami carries fibres from the septal area to the habenular nucleus.

questions.title: Which local anaesthetic is unique for its intrinsic vasoconstrictor effect?
questions.question: Which local anaesthetic is unique among clinically used local anaesthetics for producing intrinsic vasoconstriction at its site of application, rather than requiring an added vasoconstrictor?

explanations.A: Correct. Cocaine blocks presynaptic reuptake of noradrenaline in addition to blocking sodium channels. This produces local vasoconstriction as an intrinsic property of the drug itself, unlike other local anaesthetics. This dual action is exploited in ENT/nasal surgery, where topical cocaine provides both anaesthesia and haemostasis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lidocaine causes vasodilation and is typically combined with an added vasoconstrictor such as adrenaline to prolong its action, rather than possessing intrinsic vasoconstrictor activity.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Bupivacaine, like lidocaine, causes vasodilation and needs an added vasoconstrictor; it has no intrinsic vasoconstrictor effect.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Procaine similarly lacks intrinsic vasoconstrictor activity and does not share cocaine's noradrenaline-reuptake-blocking mechanism.

questions.learning_objective: State that cocaine, unlike other local anaesthetics, produces intrinsic vasoconstriction rather than requiring an added vasoconstrictor.

questions.title: Which memory system holds the opening words of a sentence while reading continues?
questions.question: While reading a sentence, the first two words are held in mind as the rest of the sentence is processed and integrated. Which memory system is responsible for this?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Long-term memory stores information over much longer timescales (days to a lifetime); it is not what actively holds the first words of a sentence for the few seconds needed to finish reading it.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Sensory memory is a very brief (sub-second), pre-attentive buffer of raw sensory input, too short-lived to hold the first words while the rest of a sentence is read.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Episodic memory stores personally experienced events over the long term, not the moment-to-moment holding of words during ongoing sentence comprehension.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Semantic memory stores general facts and word meanings long-term; it is not the active buffer holding specific just-read words during comprehension.
explanations.E: Correct. Working memory is the short-term, limited-capacity system that actively holds and manipulates information for an ongoing task. Here, it holds the sentence's first words online so they can be integrated with the words that follow. This is a classic illustration of working memory's role in language comprehension, distinct from long-term storage systems.

questions.learning_objective: State that the words held in mind at the start of a sentence, while the rest is read, are an example of working memory.

questions.title: What autonomic effect follows stimulation of the posterior hypothalamus?
questions.question: Stimulation of the posterior (lateral) hypothalamus produces which autonomic effect?

explanations.A: Correct. The posterior (lateral) hypothalamus is the principal hypothalamic centre for sympathetic outflow. Its stimulation produces tachycardia together with vasoconstriction and shivering, but not sweating. This contrasts with the anterior hypothalamus, which is chiefly associated with parasympathetic, heat-dissipating responses including sweating.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Bradycardia via parasympathetic activation is more characteristic of anterior hypothalamic stimulation, not the sympathetically-driven posterior hypothalamus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Sweating is a cholinergic sympathetic response linked to anterior hypothalamic heat-dissipating pathways, and is explicitly not produced by posterior hypothalamic stimulation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sympathetic activation from the posterior hypothalamus produces pupillary dilation (mydriasis), not constriction (miosis).

questions.learning_objective: State that stimulation of the posterior hypothalamus produces sympathetically mediated tachycardia, with vasoconstriction and shivering but not sweating.
